claims.text: Introducing a 1 vol% dispersion of Y2O3 nanoparticles into a refractory high-entropy alloy will enhance its radiation tolerance.
A 1 vol% Y2O3 nanoparticle dispersion will preserve the alloy's mechanical integrity under plasma-facing fusion-reactor conditions.
The initial refractory high-entropy alloy has a uniform microstructure.
The initial alloy has established phase stability and mechanical performance.
Interfaces between the Y2O3 nanoparticles and the alloy matrix are the structural mediator of the proposed radiation-tolerance effect.
Y2O3 nanoparticles serve as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
The nanoparticle sinks capture and annihilate irradiation-induced point defects and defect clusters.
Defect capture and annihilation at the nanoparticles limit the accumulation of radiation damage.
A 1 vol% nanoparticle dispersion does not significantly disrupt the continuous metallic matrix.
The continuous metallic matrix provides the alloy's mechanical strength.
After the specified irradiation, the Y2O3-modified alloy will have more than 30% lower defect density than the unmodified alloy.
After irradiation, the tensile strength of the modified alloy will remain within 5% of that of the unmodified alloy.
The proposed benefit will persist at temperatures up to roughly 800°C if the nanoparticle dispersion remains stable and well distributed.
Approximately 1 MeV He-ion irradiation to about 10^21 ions/m^2 is representative of plasma-facing fusion-reactor irradiation conditions.
